messages.content: What is the best month to visit Hawaii?

function.name: get_average_monthly_temperature

message.content:
The “best” time to visit Hawaii depends on what you’re looking for—mild weather, lower crowds, and better deals. For most travelers, the shoulder seasons of **April–June** and **September–November** strike the best balance:

| Month | Avg. High (°F) | Avg. Low (°F) | Notes |
|-------|----------------|---------------|-------|
| April | ~81 °F | ~68 °F | Rainfall starts to drop; still plenty of sunshine. |
| May | ~84 °F | ~70 °F | Warm but not scorching; great for outdoor activities. |
| June | ~86 °F | ~71 °F | Still comfortable before the peak‑summer heat. |
| September | ~85 °F | ~70 °F | Post‑hurricane season; sunny and relatively dry. |
| October | ~83 °F | ~69 °F | Cooler evenings; fewer tourists. |
| November | ~80 °F | ~67 °F | Early fall; mild temperatures and lower rates. |

### Why these months?
1. **Comfortable temperatures** – You’ll avoid the extreme heat of July/August and the cooler winter months (December–February) when some beaches may feel chilly.
2. **Lower humidity & rainfall** – April–June and September–November see reduced rainfall compared to the wettest months (January–March).
3. **Fewer crowds & better rates** – Peak tourist season (July–August) brings higher prices and larger crowds, while the shoulder seasons offer more relaxed vibes and often better accommodation deals.

If you’re a big fan of surfing, the winter months (December–February) bring excellent waves, especially on the North Shore. If you prefer a quieter, family-friendly trip, the shoulder seasons above are ideal. Happy planning!
